Shows the outline sketch of the River Annapolis Royal plan. Relief shown pictorially. Pen-and-ink, manuscript map. Dedicated to Lawrence Armstrong, probably by George Mitchell, deputy of David Dunbar, who was appointed surveyor general in 1728. In Beamish Murdock's: A history of Nova-Scotia, or Acadie, Volume 1, page 482, is the following: Soon after (1732) a deputy of Colonel Dunbar's as H.M. Surveyor General of woods, named George Mitchell, arrived in Annapolis, to execute his duty in Nova Scotia, and he was directed to make a survey of the lands upon the Annapolis River. Imperfect: Discoloration, staining throughout, torn at fold lines, hemmed at edges with green cloth, and mounted on cloth. Available also through the Library of Congress Web site as a raster image.
